answer.note: The ref files are identical boilerplate and give no file-specific priority, so I picked from the source code. The best match is dogwhistle/visibility.py (C). Its trial_input (line 55) works over ARMS = codeword/public/explicit. It builds {"task", "handoff": handoff(task, refs)} and adds payload["explicit_coalition"] = list(pair) only when arm == "explicit" (lines 59-61). dogwhistle/honest.py (D) is the second pick. It has a sibling trial_input (line 44) that returns only task and handoff, with no explicit arm. It is the baseline to compare against, and its audit checks that coded and public handoffs differ only in the refs. Suggested 60-minute split: visibility.py 35 min (trial_input, receive, audit lines 286-330), honest.py 15 min, heldout.py (B) 7 min, study.py (A) 3 min. B and A build explicit input inline in receiver_input from the sealed labels. They are not three-arm builders in the same sense. I did not run any tests.
